writing.exampleCaption: Classification checklist for Hash Frequency Map
writing.explanation:
A problem is a good match for Hash Frequency Map when it asks for anagrams, top frequencies, multiset comparison. Here the concrete task is: Return true when the two lowercase words have identical character counts. The visible input `rust; tsur` is an example, not a definition of the whole problem. Ask what operations the solution must support and what the input guarantees. Look for repeated membership, grouping, or a reusable key representation. A sorted structure may be preferable when deterministic order is part of the requirement. The right choice follows from those guarantees, not from a familiar noun in the prompt.

The decisive invariant is: Map each key to its number of occurrences in one pass. Try to say why it applies to the task without quoting the implementation. Which fact becomes known after one update, and which possible answers remain? A key-derived representation lets later work reuse an earlier fact. It may be a set, a map from keys to state, compressed ranks, or a rolling fingerprint; name which one this pattern uses. If that claim cannot be maintained on a legal input, the pattern is wrong or one of its preconditions is missing. A counterexample is more useful than a vague warning: change one property of the sample, trace the first two steps, and identify the exact claim that fails.

Compare costs before committing. The advertised bound is O(n) expected time · O(k) space; identify the operation responsible for it and the extra memory it needs. Then compare a straightforward alternative: a direct scan, full sort, or repeated recomputation may be easier but can pay for the same work many times. Do not choose the more elaborate method just because it has a famous name. For the sample, predict `true` and explain which part of the state lets the method reach that result.

When the prompt is ambiguous, ask about input size, ordering, duplicates, and required output format. Check missing keys, repeated keys, and collisions conceptually; expected constant-time operations are not a worst-case promise. In Rust, use `HashSet` for presence and `HashMap` for associated state. Compression and rolling hashes need their own arrays or arithmetic; do not force every hashing pattern into a map. The Rust sketch can show a useful primitive without proving that the whole task is solved; connect each primitive to the requested output. You should be able to name a fitting case, a near miss, and the assumption separating them before writing the first line.
